question: What title does Paul give God?
explanation: Paul calls Him the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort.

question: Why does God comfort believers in all their tribulation?
choices: So they may avoid all sorrow
So they may boast in strength
So they may return to Jerusalem
explanation: God comforts believers so they can comfort others in trouble.

question: In whom are all the promises of God yes and amen?
explanation: Paul says all God's promises are yes and amen in Christ.

question: What does Paul say God has given as an earnest in believers' hearts?
explanation: God has sealed believers and given the Spirit as the earnest.

question: Why had Paul not yet come again to Corinth?
explanation: Paul says he delayed his visit to spare them.

question: What did Paul say should be done for the repentant offender?
explanation: Paul says they should forgive and comfort him.

question: Why does Paul say believers should forgive?
choices: Lest Satan should get an advantage
explanation: Paul says forgiveness prevents Satan from gaining an advantage.

question: What does God always cause Paul and his companions to do in Christ?
explanation: God always causes them to triumph in Christ.

question: What does Paul say the apostles are unto God?
explanation: They are a sweet savour of Christ unto God.

question: How does Paul say he speaks in Christ?
choices: As of sincerity, as of God
explanation: Paul says he speaks in Christ sincerely, as from God.

question: What does Paul call the Corinthians?
explanation: Paul says, 'Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men.'

question: Paul calls the Corinthians the epistle of Christ. With what does he say it was written?
choices: The Spirit of the living God
explanation: It was written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God.

question: Paul says the spirit giveth life. What does he say the letter does?
explanation: The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

question: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is what?
explanation: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

question: Into what are believers changed from glory to glory?
explanation: Believers are changed into the same image from glory to glory.

question: Why does Paul say he does not faint in ministry?
explanation: He does not faint because he has received mercy.

question: Who has blinded the minds of them which believe not?
explanation: Paul says the god of this world has blinded unbelievers' minds.

question: Where is the treasure placed?
explanation: The treasure is in earthen vessels so God's power is seen.

question: What happens to the outward man?
explanation: Though the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day.

question: What does Paul say believers should look at?
choices: The things which are not seen
explanation: Believers are to look at the unseen, eternal things.

question: What does Paul call the earthly body?
explanation: He calls the earthly body our earthly house of this tabernacle.

question: How do believers walk?
explanation: Believers walk by faith, not by sight.

question: Before whose judgment seat must all appear?
explanation: All must appear before the judgment seat of Christ.

question: If any man be in Christ, he is what?
explanation: If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature.

question: What ministry has God given believers?
explanation: God has given believers the ministry of reconciliation.

question: What does Paul say is the accepted time and day?
explanation: Now is the accepted time; now is the day of salvation.

question: What does Paul say believers should not be unequally yoked with?
explanation: Believers should not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers.

question: Which temple does Paul say believers are?
explanation: Believers are the temple of the living God.

question: What promise does God make?
choices: I will be a Father unto you
explanation: God promises to be a Father to His people.

question: What does Paul urge believers to cleanse themselves from?
choices: All filthiness of flesh and spirit
explanation: Believers should cleanse themselves from all filthiness of flesh and spirit.

question: Who brought Paul comfort by his coming?
explanation: God comforted Paul by the coming of Titus.

question: What kind of sorrow works repentance not to be repented of?
explanation: Godly sorrow works repentance to salvation.

question: What does worldly sorrow work?
explanation: Worldly sorrow works death.

question: How did Paul describe his feeling toward the Corinthians after hearing Titus' report?
explanation: Paul rejoiced in their repentance and obedience.

question: Which churches are praised for generosity?
explanation: Paul highlights the grace of God given to the churches of Macedonia.

question: To whom did the Macedonian believers first give themselves?
explanation: They first gave their own selves to the Lord.

question: What example of giving does Paul give?
choices: Christ became poor for your sakes
explanation: Though Christ was rich, yet for believers' sakes He became poor.

question: According to 2 Corinthians 8:12, giving is accepted according to what?
explanation: Giving is accepted according to what a person has.

question: Who is described as being earnest in the matter of the collection?
explanation: Titus is commended for his earnest care.

question: How should each person give?
choices: As he purposes in his heart
explanation: Each should give as he purposes in his heart.

question: Whom does God love?
explanation: God loves a cheerful giver.

question: What is God able to make abound toward believers?
explanation: God is able to make all grace abound toward them.

question: Who gives seed to the sower and bread for food?
explanation: God ministers seed to the sower and bread for food.

question: What does generous ministry cause?
explanation: It causes many thanksgivings unto God.

question: What kind of weapons does Paul say believers use in warfare?
explanation: Their weapons are not carnal but mighty through God.

question: What do these spiritual weapons pull down?
explanation: They are mighty to the pulling down of strong holds.

question: What does Paul say believers should bring into captivity?
choices: Every thought to the obedience of Christ
explanation: Every thought should be brought into captivity to Christ's obedience.

question: What does Paul say he will not boast of?
explanation: Paul will not boast of things beyond his measure, that is, of other men's labours.

question: Paul says that anyone who glories should glory in whom?
explanation: He that glories, let him glory in the Lord.

question: What does Paul fear the Corinthians' minds may be corrupted from, as Eve was beguiled?
choices: The simplicity that is in Christ
explanation: Paul fears they may be corrupted from the simplicity in Christ.

question: What does Satan transform himself into?
explanation: Satan transforms himself into an angel of light.

question: What does Paul say he preached to the Corinthians freely?
explanation: Paul preached the gospel of God to them freely.

question: What did Paul receive from the Jews five times?
explanation: Five times he received forty stripes save one.

question: What does Paul say he will glory in if he must glory?
choices: The things which concern his infirmities
explanation: Paul says he will glory in the things that concern his infirmities.

question: Paul tells of a man in Christ who was caught up to which heaven?
explanation: Paul says he knew a man in Christ who was caught up to the third heaven.

question: What was given to Paul lest he should be exalted above measure?
explanation: A thorn in the flesh was given to humble him.

question: How many times did Paul ask the Lord to take the thorn away?
explanation: Paul sought the Lord three times about it.

question: What did the Lord say is sufficient for Paul?
explanation: The Lord answered, 'My grace is sufficient for thee.'

question: When does Paul say he is strong?
explanation: Paul says when he is weak, then he is strong.

question: How many witnesses does Paul say establish every word?
explanation: Every word shall be established by two or three witnesses.

question: What does Paul tell the Corinthians to examine?
choices: Themselves, whether they be in the faith
explanation: He tells them to examine themselves whether they are in the faith.

question: Paul says Christ is not weak toward the Corinthians. What does he say Christ is in them?
explanation: Christ is not weak, but mighty in them.

question: What does Paul tell the Corinthians to do as he says farewell?
choices: Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind
explanation: Paul tells them to be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind and live in peace.

question: What threefold blessing closes the letter?
choices: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost
explanation: Paul ends with a Trinitarian blessing of grace, love, and fellowship.

question: By whose meekness and gentleness does Paul beseech the Corinthians?
explanation: Now I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ.

question: What do his critics say about Paul's bodily presence?
explanation: His letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak.

question: Though Paul walks in the flesh, what does he not do?
explanation: Though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.

question: Who is approved, says Paul?
explanation: Not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.

question: How do Paul's critics describe his letters?
explanation: His letters, say they, are weighty and powerful.

question: Paul says in presence he is base among them, but absent he is what?
explanation: Who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you.

question: Paul casts down every high thing that exalteth itself against what?
explanation: Every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God.

question: Paul is ready to revenge all disobedience when what is fulfilled?
explanation: Having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.

question: Paul asks whether they look on things after what?
explanation: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance?

question: The authority the Lord gave Paul was for edification and not for what?
explanation: Our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction.

question: What will Paul be in deed when present, as he is in letters when absent?
choices: Such as he is in word
explanation: Such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such will we be also in deed when we are present.

question: What does Paul say of those who measure themselves among themselves?
explanation: They measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise.

question: What does Paul say he could boast somewhat more of, and not be ashamed?
explanation: Though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, I should not be ashamed.

question: How far does Paul say God's measure reached?
explanation: According to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you.

question: Where does Paul hope to preach when their faith is increased?
explanation: To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you.

question: What does Paul say to a man who trusts that he is Christ's?
choices: As he is Christ's, so are we
explanation: As he is Christ's, even so are we Christ's.

question: What does Paul say he does not want to seem to do by letters?
explanation: That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.

question: Paul hopes to be enlarged by them when what is increased?
explanation: Having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you.

question: Paul says he came as far as Corinth by doing what?
explanation: We are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ.

question: What do critics say of Paul's speech?
explanation: His bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.

question: Whom does Paul say they dare not compare themselves with?
explanation: We dare not compare ourselves with some that commend themselves.

question: What do some think of Paul and his companions?
choices: That they walk according to the flesh
explanation: Some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh.

question: To whom has Paul espoused the Corinthians, to present as a chaste virgin?
explanation: I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

question: How many times was Paul beaten with rods?
explanation: Thrice was I beaten with rods.

question: What does Paul say happened to him once?
explanation: Once was I stoned.

question: How did Paul escape from Damascus?
choices: Let down in a basket through a window
explanation: Through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.

question: What comes upon Paul daily besides the things without?
choices: The care of all the churches
explanation: That which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.

question: Paul says he is the seed of whom?
explanation: Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.

question: How long was Paul in the deep?
explanation: A night and a day I have been in the deep.

question: What does Paul call those who transform themselves into apostles of Christ?
explanation: Such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

question: Whom did Paul rob by taking wages to serve the Corinthians?
explanation: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service.

question: How many times did Paul suffer shipwreck?
explanation: Thrice I suffered shipwreck.

question: Who supplied what Paul lacked while he was with the Corinthians?
explanation: That which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied.

question: No man shall stop Paul's boasting in the regions of where?
explanation: No man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia.

question: Why does Paul keep doing as he does about wages?
choices: To cut off occasion from those who desire it
explanation: That I may cut off occasion from them which desire occasion.

question: Paul supposes he was not a whit behind whom?
explanation: I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

question: Paul admits he is rude in speech, but not in what?
explanation: Though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge.

question: If a man preaches another Jesus, what might the Corinthians well do?
explanation: If he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, ye might well bear with him.

question: What does Paul say the Corinthians suffer gladly, seeing they are wise?
explanation: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.

question: According to what shall the end of Satan's ministers be?
explanation: Whose end shall be according to their works.

question: Under which king was the governor in Damascus who sought Paul?
explanation: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city.

question: Which does Paul list among his perils?
explanation: In perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city.

question: How does Paul say he speaks in this boasting?
explanation: That which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly.

question: Paul says many glory after what?
explanation: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.

question: Paul says he is more than the ministers of Christ in what?
explanation: In labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

question: How does Paul describe his stripes?
explanation: In stripes above measure.

question: What does Paul say he will keep himself from being to the Corinthians?
explanation: In all things I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself.

question: Paul asks if he refuses support because he loves them not. Who knows?
explanation: Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.

question: Which does Paul say the Corinthians endure from a man?
explanation: If a man smite you on the face.

question: Which hardships does Paul list together at the end of the list?
explanation: In fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

question: Whom does Paul call blessed for evermore?
choices: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
explanation: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is blessed for evermore, knoweth that I lie not.

question: What does Paul want to present the Corinthians as to Christ?
explanation: That I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

question: If men think Paul a fool, what does he ask of them?
choices: To receive him as a fool
explanation: Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.

question: What does Paul say was often his portion besides labours and stripes?
explanation: In prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

question: What does Paul ask the Corinthians to bear with him in?
explanation: Would to God ye could bear with me a little in my folly.

question: What did the governor keep the city of the Damascenes with?
explanation: The governor kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison.

question: Why does Paul say he abased himself?
choices: That the Corinthians might be exalted
explanation: Have I committed an offence in abasing myself that ye might be exalted?

question: How does Paul say he is jealous over the Corinthians?
explanation: I am jealous over you with godly jealousy.

question: False ministers are transformed as the ministers of what?
explanation: His ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness.

question: What might a false preacher bring that Paul says they had not accepted?
explanation: Or another gospel, which ye have not accepted.

question: Which hardships does Paul list with fastings often?
explanation: In hunger and thirst, in fastings often.

question: Which three claims does Paul match against the false apostles?
choices: Hebrew, Israelite and seed of Abraham
explanation: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.

question: What did the man caught up into paradise hear?
explanation: He heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

question: What does Paul call the thorn in the flesh?
explanation: A thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me.

question: Why does Paul gladly glory in his infirmities?
choices: That the power of Christ may rest upon him
explanation: Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

question: The Lord said his strength is made perfect in what?
explanation: My strength is made perfect in weakness.

question: Whom did Paul desire to go to Corinth, with a brother?
explanation: I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother.

question: What does Paul say he seeks from the Corinthians?
explanation: I seek not yours, but you.

question: Whether the man was in the body or out, who knoweth?
explanation: Whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth.

question: Into what was the man also caught up?
explanation: He was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words.

question: Of himself Paul will not glory, but in what?
explanation: Of myself I will not glory, but in mine infirmities.

question: Why does Paul forbear to glory?
choices: Lest any man think of him above what he seeth
explanation: I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me to be.

question: Who does Paul say compelled him to glory like a fool?
explanation: I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me.

question: What was wrought among the Corinthians as the signs of an apostle?
explanation: The signs of an apostle were wrought among you in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.

question: In what were the Corinthians inferior to other churches?
choices: Paul was not burdensome to them
explanation: Wherein were ye inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you?

question: How many times is Paul ready to come to them?
explanation: Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you.

question: Who ought to lay up for whom, says Paul?
explanation: The children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

question: What will Paul very gladly do for them?
explanation: I will very gladly spend and be spent for you.

question: Paul asks if he and Titus walked in the same what?
explanation: Walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?

question: How long ago was the man caught up to the third heaven?
explanation: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago.

question: Paul says they do all things for their what?
explanation: We do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

question: Which does Paul fear to find among the Corinthians?
explanation: Lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults.

question: Of what had many not repented?
explanation: Many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness.

question: Who does Paul fear will humble him among them when he comes again?
explanation: When I come again, my God will humble me among you.

question: What did some say of Paul, being crafty?
choices: That he caught them with guile
explanation: Being crafty, I caught you with guile.

question: What happens the more abundantly Paul loves them?
explanation: The more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved.

question: Paul will come to visions and revelations of whom?
explanation: I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

question: For whose sake does Paul take pleasure in infirmities?
explanation: I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake.

question: How does Paul describe the one who was caught up to the third heaven?
explanation: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago.

question: Before whom does Paul say they speak, not excusing themselves?
explanation: Think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ.

question: Christ was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by what?
explanation: Though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God.

question: How does Paul tell them to greet one another?
explanation: Greet one another with an holy kiss.

question: How many times is Paul coming to them?
explanation: This is the third time I am coming to you.

question: What did the Corinthians seek proof of?
explanation: Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me.

question: What does Paul warn he will not do if he comes again?
explanation: If I come again, I will not spare.

question: Christ is in them, says Paul, unless they be what?
explanation: Know ye not that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?

question: What does Paul say they can do nothing against?
explanation: We can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.

question: Why does Paul write these things while absent?
choices: So the letter will be longer
So he need not use sharpness when present
explanation: I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness.

question: What will be with them if they live in peace?
choices: The God of love and peace
explanation: Live in peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.

question: Paul prays they do no evil, not that they should appear what?
explanation: I pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we should appear approved.

question: What does Paul say he wishes for the Corinthians?
explanation: This also we wish, even your perfection.

question: Who salute the Corinthians?
explanation: All the saints salute you.

question: What does Paul trust they will know about him?
explanation: I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.

question: Paul warns he will not spare those who have what?
explanation: I write to them which heretofore have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare.

question: When are Paul and his companions glad?
choices: When they are weak and the Corinthians strong
explanation: We are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong.

question: Paul says the power the Lord gave him is for edification and not for what?
explanation: The power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.

question: In their deep poverty, the Macedonians abounded unto the riches of what?
explanation: The abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.

question: The gift Paul collected was for the ministering to whom?
explanation: The Macedonians prayed Paul to take upon him the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.

question: Paul says he speaks of giving to prove what of the Corinthians?
explanation: Paul writes to prove the sincerity of their love.

question: Paul urges those who abound in faith and knowledge to abound in what also?
explanation: As ye abound in every thing, see that ye abound in this grace also.

question: How far did the Macedonians give, by Paul's record?
explanation: To their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves.

question: What does Paul ask the Corinthians to show to the messengers and the churches?
explanation: Shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love.

question: How does Paul describe Titus to the Corinthians?
explanation: Titus is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you.

question: What did the Macedonians pray Paul with much intreaty to do?
explanation: They prayed us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.

question: What did Paul desire Titus to do among the Corinthians, as he had begun?
explanation: We desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also.

question: Paul wants their readiness to will matched by what?
choices: A performance out of what they have
explanation: As there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which ye have.

question: What does Paul say he wants between the Corinthians and the saints in need?
explanation: Your abundance may be a supply for their want, that there may be equality.

question: Which things does Paul say the Corinthians already abound in?
explanation: Ye abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence.

question: How is the brother sent with Titus described?
choices: His praise is in the gospel in all the churches
He is an elder of Jerusalem
He is a kinsman of Titus
explanation: The brother whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches.

question: What did Paul want to avoid in handling the abundance?
choices: That any man should blame him
explanation: Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us.

question: What occasion led Paul to speak of giving to the Corinthians?
explanation: I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others.

question: What does the gift, as Paul administers it, declare about the Corinthians?
explanation: The grace administered by us is to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind.

question: Whom does Paul call the messengers of the churches?
explanation: The brethren are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.

question: How did Titus go to Corinth?
explanation: Being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.

question: Who put the same earnest care for the Corinthians into Titus's heart?
explanation: Thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

question: How long ago had the Corinthians begun to be forward in this?
explanation: Who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.

question: What does Scripture say of him that had gathered much?
choices: He had to give it away
explanation: He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack.

question: Who chose the brother to travel with Paul with this grace?
explanation: The brother was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace.

question: Besides in the sight of the Lord, in whose sight does Paul provide honest things?
explanation: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

question: Why was the second brother much more diligent in this matter?
choices: Great confidence Paul had in the Corinthians
explanation: Much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.

question: Whose abundance may later be a supply for the Corinthians' want?
explanation: Their abundance also may be a supply for your want.

question: Paul asks them to show proof of their love and of what?
explanation: Shew ye the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.

question: Paul tells of the grace of God bestowed on which churches?
explanation: We do you to wit of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia.

question: In what did the Macedonians' abundance of joy abound?
explanation: In a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy abounded.

question: Besides the Lord, to whom did the Macedonians give themselves, by God's will?
explanation: They first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.

question: What does Paul say he does NOT mean by the collection?
choices: That others be eased and the Corinthians burdened
explanation: I mean not that other men be eased, and ye burdened.

question: What had Paul often proved about the third man he sent?
choices: He was diligent in many things
explanation: Our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things.

question: What shall he which soweth sparingly reap?
explanation: He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly.

question: What does Paul thank God for at the close of the chapter?
explanation: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.

question: Whom did Paul send ahead to Corinth?
explanation: Yet have I sent the brethren, lest our boasting of you should be in vain.

question: To whom did Paul boast that Achaia was ready a year ago?
explanation: I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago.

question: Why did Paul send the brethren ahead?
choices: So the Corinthians would be ready
explanation: Lest our boasting of you should be in vain, that ye may be ready.

question: What did Paul fear if the Macedonians found Corinth unprepared?
choices: That the gift would be lost
explanation: If they of Macedonia find you unprepared, we should be ashamed.

question: Paul wanted the bounty ready as bounty, and not as of what?
explanation: That the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.

question: What remaineth for ever, as it is written of him who gives to the poor?
explanation: He hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever.

question: God makes grace abound so they may abound to what?
explanation: That ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work.

question: God will multiply their seed sown and increase what?
explanation: He multiplieth your seed sown, and increaseth the fruits of your righteousness.

question: Besides causing thanksgivings, what does this service supply?
explanation: The administration of this service not only supplieth the want of the saints.

question: For what do the saints glorify God because of this ministration?
choices: The Corinthians' professed subjection to the gospel
explanation: They glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ.

question: What do the saints do for the Corinthians, longing after them?
explanation: By their prayer for you, which long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you.

question: How long ago had Achaia been ready, as Paul boasted?
explanation: I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago.

question: What had the Corinthians' zeal done to very many?
explanation: Your zeal hath provoked very many.

question: Besides the saints, to whom does the Corinthians' liberal distribution reach?
explanation: For your liberal distribution unto them, and unto all men.

question: Paul fears being ashamed in what, if they are unprepared?
explanation: We should be ashamed in this same confident boasting.

question: What does Paul say he knows about the Corinthians?
explanation: For I know the forwardness of your mind.

question: What does Paul say about writing to them of the ministering to the saints?
explanation: As touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.

question: Who is named with Paul as the sender of this letter?
explanation: The letter opens with Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother.

question: By whose will does Paul say he is an apostle of Jesus Christ?
explanation: Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God.

question: What does Paul wish for the Corinthians from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ?
explanation: Paul writes, Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

question: Where did the trouble come to Paul that pressed him out of measure?
explanation: Paul would not have them ignorant of the trouble which came to them in Asia.

question: In whom does Paul say they learned to trust instead of in themselves?
explanation: They had the sentence of death in themselves, that they should not trust in themselves, but in God which raiseth the dead.

question: By whom does Paul say our consolation also aboundeth?
explanation: As the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.

question: Who does Paul say stablisheth him with the Corinthians in Christ and hath anointed them?
explanation: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God.

question: If Paul is afflicted, what does he say it is for?
explanation: Whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation.

question: How does Paul describe the trouble that came to him in Asia?
choices: A trouble he brought on himself
Pressed out of measure, above strength
A small delay on the road
explanation: They were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that they despaired even of life.

question: What does Paul say the Corinthians do to help him, so that many give thanks?
explanation: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

question: What does Paul call his rejoicing?
choices: The letters of commendation he carried
The miracles done by his hands
explanation: For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity we have had our conversation in the world.

question: What does Paul say he writes to the Corinthians, and nothing else?
explanation: We write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge.

question: In which day does Paul say the Corinthians are his rejoicing, even as he is theirs?
choices: The day of the Lord Jesus
explanation: Ye are our rejoicing, even as we are yours in the day of the Lord Jesus.

question: After Macedonia, toward what land did Paul plan to be brought on his way by the Corinthians?
explanation: He planned to come again out of Macedonia unto them, and of them to be brought on his way toward Judaea.

question: What did Paul hope the Corinthians might have from his planned visit?
explanation: In this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit.

question: Who does Paul say was preached among the Corinthians by himself, Silvanus and Timotheus?
choices: The Son of God, Jesus Christ
explanation: The Son of God, Jesus Christ, was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus.

question: What does Paul trust that God will yet do, having delivered them from so great a death?
explanation: He delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us.

question: Whom does Paul call for a record upon his soul that he came not yet to Corinth to spare them?
explanation: Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.

question: What does Paul say he and his companions are to the Corinthians, not lords over their faith?
explanation: Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy.

question: Besides Corinth, whose saints does the opening address include?
explanation: The letter is unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia.

question: Paul says the Corinthians are partakers of the sufferings. Of what shall they be partakers also?
explanation: As ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.

question: What did Paul and his companions despair of in the trouble in Asia?
explanation: They were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that they despaired even of life.

question: For what, through many persons, does Paul say thanks may be given by many?
explanation: That for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

question: Not with fleshly wisdom, but by what did Paul say he lived in the world?
explanation: In simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world.

question: Where did Paul plan to pass by the Corinthians into, and then come again out of?
explanation: He planned to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you.

question: Paul asked if his plans were purposed according to what, so that with him there should be yea yea, and nay nay?
explanation: Do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay?

question: On what does Paul rest his claim that his word toward them was not yea and nay?
explanation: But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.

question: Which two men does Paul name as preaching Christ with him among the Corinthians?
explanation: The Son of God was preached among you by me and Silvanus and Timotheus.

question: All the promises of God in Christ are yea and Amen unto what?
explanation: All the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.

question: Paul says that by what do the Corinthians stand?
explanation: We are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand.

question: Besides stablishing and anointing them, what does Paul say God hath also done to believers?
explanation: God hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

question: At which city did Paul say a door was opened to him to preach Christ's gospel?
explanation: When I came to Troas to preach Christ's gospel, a door was opened unto me of the Lord.

question: Whom did Paul not find at Troas, so that he had no rest in his spirit?
explanation: I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother.

question: Where did Paul go after taking his leave of those at Troas?
explanation: Taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia.

question: How did Paul say he wrote to the Corinthians out of much affliction?
explanation: Out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears.

question: Why did Paul say the offender should be forgiven and comforted?
choices: Lest he be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow
explanation: Ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

question: What did Paul say of the punishment inflicted on the offender by many?
explanation: Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.

question: What did Paul ask the Corinthians to confirm toward the offender?
explanation: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.

question: What did Paul say he wrote to find out about the Corinthians?
choices: Whether they would send a gift
Whether they were obedient in all things
Whether they had left the church
explanation: For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.

question: In whose person did Paul say he forgave for the Corinthians' sakes?
explanation: For your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ.

question: Why did Paul say he decided not to come to them again in heaviness?
choices: He would not make them sorry
explanation: But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.

question: Why did Paul say he wrote with many tears?
choices: That they might know his abundant love
That they might leave the city
explanation: I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.

question: What was opened to Paul by the Lord when he came to Troas?
explanation: When I came to Troas to preach Christ's gospel, a door was opened unto me of the Lord.

question: What does Paul say God maketh manifest by the apostles in every place?
explanation: God maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.

question: To those who perish, what does Paul say the apostles are the savour of?
explanation: To the one we are the savour of death unto death.

question: To those who are saved, what does Paul say the apostles are the savour of?
explanation: To the other the savour of life unto life.

question: Which question does Paul ask after speaking of the savour of death and life?
choices: Who is sufficient for these things?
Who hath known the mind of the Lord?
explanation: And who is sufficient for these things?

question: What does Paul say he does not do, as many do, with the word of God?
explanation: We are not as many, which corrupt the word of God.

question: Paul says: if he makes the Corinthians sorry, who maketh him glad?
choices: The same which is made sorry by him
explanation: If I make you sorry, who is he then that maketh me glad, but the same which is made sorry by me?

question: Paul wrote lest, when he came, he should have sorrow from whom?
choices: Them of whom he ought to rejoice
explanation: I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice.

question: Of the one who caused grief, why does Paul say he has grieved him only in part?
choices: That he may not overcharge them all
That he may keep the peace in Rome
That he may hide the matter
That he may rest at Troas
explanation: If any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.

question: Paul says his joy is the joy of whom?
explanation: I have confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.

question: In whose sight does Paul say he speaks in Christ?
explanation: In the sight of God speak we in Christ.

question: Where does Paul say the Corinthians' epistle is written, not in tables of stone?
choices: In fleshy tables of the heart
In a book of the law
explanation: The epistle of Christ is written not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.

question: Who does Paul say hath made the apostles able ministers of the new testament?
explanation: Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; our sufficiency is of God.

question: What did Moses put over his face?
explanation: Moses put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished.

question: Whose face could the children of Israel not stedfastly behold for its glory?
explanation: The children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance.

question: In what is the epistle known and read of all men written?
explanation: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men.

question: Of whom does Paul say our sufficiency is?
explanation: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God.

question: Paul says God made them ministers of the new testament, not of the letter, but of what?
explanation: Not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

question: Through whom does Paul say they have such trust toward God?
explanation: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward.

question: Why did Moses put a vail over his face, according to Paul?
choices: So Israel could not look to the end of what was abolished
So he could hide his fear
explanation: Moses put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished.

question: In the reading of what does Paul say the same vail remains untaken away?
explanation: Until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament.

question: When Moses is read, where does Paul say the vail is?
explanation: Even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart.

question: What does Paul say shall happen when it shall turn to the Lord?
choices: The law shall be done away
The vail shall be taken away
explanation: Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

question: Why does Paul say he uses great plainness of speech?
explanation: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech.

question: Paul asks whether they need, as some others, what for the Corinthians?
explanation: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you?

question: Upon what was the ministration of death written and engraven?
explanation: The ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious.

question: Which ministration does Paul say exceeds in glory the ministration of condemnation?
explanation: If the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

question: Paul says if that which is done away was glorious, much more is what glorious?
explanation: If that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious.

question: What did Paul say was blinded?
explanation: But their minds were blinded.

question: In whom does Paul say the vail is done away?
explanation: The same vail remaineth untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.

question: With what kind of face do believers behold as in a glass the glory of the Lord?
explanation: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image.

question: By whom are believers changed from glory to glory?
explanation: We are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.

question: What does Paul say the Lord is?
explanation: Now the Lord is that Spirit.

question: Whom does Paul say he and his companions preach, not themselves?
explanation: We preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.

question: What does Paul say he who raised up the Lord Jesus will do for us?
explanation: He which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus.

question: What happens to the inward man day by day?
explanation: Though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.

question: What does Paul call his affliction which works a far more exceeding weight of glory?
explanation: Our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.

question: Why does Paul say we have this treasure in earthen vessels?
choices: That the excellency of the power may be of God
That it may be kept in the temple
explanation: We have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.

question: Paul says he is troubled on every side, yet not what?
explanation: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed.

question: Paul says he is persecuted, but not what?
explanation: Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed.

question: Paul says he is cast down, but not what?
explanation: Cast down, but not destroyed.

question: Paul says death worketh in the apostles. What worketh in the Corinthians?
explanation: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

question: Paul says he has the same spirit of faith; what does he say, because he believes?
explanation: We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak.

question: In what has God shined, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God?
explanation: God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts.

question: Who does Paul say is the image of God?
explanation: The light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God.

question: Paul says they have renounced the hidden things of what?
explanation: We have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty.

question: Paul says they are perplexed, but not in what?
explanation: We are perplexed, but not in despair.

question: Paul says the things which are seen are what?
explanation: The things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

question: What does Paul say they bear about in the body always?
choices: The dying of the Lord Jesus
explanation: Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus.

question: Paul says they do not handle the word of God how?
explanation: Nor handling the word of God deceitfully.

question: To what will abundant grace redound through the thanksgiving of many?
explanation: That the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.

question: Lest what should shine unto those who believe not?
choices: The light of the glorious gospel of Christ
explanation: The god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ should shine unto them.

question: In the face of whom is the knowledge of the glory of God?
explanation: To give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

question: Paul says death works in the body that the life of Jesus might be made manifest in our what?
explanation: That the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

question: Paul says God who raised up Jesus shall present the apostles together with whom?
explanation: He which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you.

question: If our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, what do we have?
choices: A building of God, not made with hands
A place of rest on earth
explanation: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

question: What are the apostles, as though God did beseech you by them?
explanation: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us.

question: What does Paul say constraineth us?
explanation: For the love of Christ constraineth us.

question: Who hath wrought us for the selfsame thing, and given the earnest of the Spirit?
explanation: He that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

question: Who does Paul say knew no sin?
explanation: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin.

question: Whilst we are at home in the body, from whom are we absent?
explanation: Whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord.

question: Where is the building of God, eternal?
explanation: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

question: With what do the apostles groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon?
choices: Their house which is from heaven
explanation: In this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven.

question: Paul wants mortality to be swallowed up of what?
explanation: That mortality might be swallowed up of life.

question: Whether present or absent, what does Paul say they labour to be?
explanation: Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.

question: According to what shall every one receive the things done in his body?
choices: That he hath done, good or bad
explanation: That every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

question: Knowing the terror of the Lord, what do the apostles do?
explanation: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.

question: Paul judges that if one died for all, then were all what?
explanation: We thus judge that if one died for all, then were all dead.

question: Paul says Christ died for all, that those who live should live unto whom?
choices: Him which died for them, and rose again
explanation: That they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.

question: Paul says God was in Christ, reconciling whom unto himself?
explanation: God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself.

question: What does God not impute to them, in reconciling the world?
explanation: Not imputing their trespasses unto them.

question: Praying in Christ's stead, what does Paul beg them to be?
explanation: We pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.

question: What does Paul say are become new, when any man is in Christ?
explanation: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

question: Paul says we are willing rather to be absent from the body and present with whom?
explanation: We are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.

question: Paul says that being clothed, we shall not be found what?
explanation: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

question: What does Paul say those in this tabernacle do, being burdened?
explanation: We that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened.

question: Paul says he gives the Corinthians occasion to glory, that they may answer those who glory in what?
explanation: That ye may have somewhat to answer them which glory in appearance, and not in heart.

question: Paul says if he is beside himself, it is to whom?
explanation: For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause.

question: Paul says henceforth they know no man after what?
explanation: Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh.

question: Besides to God, where does Paul trust the apostles are made manifest?
explanation: We are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.

question: Of what has God committed the word to the apostles?
explanation: Hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.

question: Paul says God made Christ to be sin for us, that we might be made what in him?
explanation: That we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

question: Who does Paul say hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ?
explanation: All things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ.

question: Before what must we all appear, according to Paul?
explanation: We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.

question: What does Paul say light has no communion with?
explanation: What communion hath light with darkness?

question: With whom does Paul ask what concord Christ hath?
explanation: What concord hath Christ with Belial?

question: What does the Lord say to those who come out from among them?
explanation: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord.

question: What should the Corinthians not receive in vain?
explanation: We beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.

question: God says he will dwell in them, and do what else?
explanation: I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

question: Paul gives no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not what?
explanation: Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed.

question: Paul says he is sorrowful, yet always what?
explanation: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing.

question: Paul says he is poor, yet doing what?
explanation: As poor, yet making many rich.

question: Paul says he is dying, and behold what?
explanation: As dying, and, behold, we live.

question: Paul says his mouth is open, and what is enlarged?
explanation: O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.

question: Paul says the Corinthians are not straitened in him but in what?
explanation: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.

question: Speaking as to his children, what does Paul ask the Corinthians to be as a recompence?
explanation: Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be ye also enlarged.

question: In what does Paul say they approve themselves as ministers of God, listing afflictions?
explanation: In all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses.

question: What does Paul ask that righteousness has with unrighteousness?
explanation: What fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?

question: Paul says he approves himself by the armour of righteousness on what?
choices: The right hand and on the left
explanation: By the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left.

question: Paul says he is as a deceiver, and yet what?
explanation: As deceivers, and yet true.

question: Paul says he is as unknown, and yet what?
explanation: As unknown, and yet well known.

question: Paul says he is chastened, and not what?
explanation: As chastened, and not killed.

question: Paul says he is as having nothing, and yet what?
explanation: As having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

question: Which hardship does Paul list among those he endures, along with stripes?
explanation: In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings.

question: By what does Paul say he commends himself, along with the Holy Ghost?
explanation: By the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned.

question: What does the Lord say he will do if they touch not the unclean thing?
explanation: Touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you.

question: Who says he will be a Father unto them, and they shall be his sons and daughters?
explanation: And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

question: Where did Paul say, when they were come there, their flesh had no rest?
explanation: When we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side.

question: Paul says without were fightings, and within were what?
explanation: Without were fightings, within were fears.

question: Who does Paul say comforteth those that are cast down?
explanation: God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus.

question: What does Paul say they have not done to any man?
explanation: We have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.

question: Paul says the Corinthians are in his heart to do what?
explanation: Ye are in our hearts to die and live with you.

question: Paul says he is filled with comfort and exceeding joyful in what?
explanation: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.

question: What did Titus tell Paul of the Corinthians, along with their mourning?
explanation: He told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.

question: With what did Paul say he made the Corinthians sorry?
explanation: Though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent.

question: Paul rejoices not that they were made sorry, but that they sorrowed to what?
explanation: I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance.

question: Paul says godly sorrow works repentance to what?
choices: Salvation not to be repented of
explanation: Godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of.

question: Whose spirit was refreshed by the Corinthians?
explanation: We joyed for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.

question: Which of these did Paul say godly sorrow worked in the Corinthians?
explanation: What carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear.

question: Paul says the sorrow of the world worketh what?
explanation: The sorrow of the world worketh death.

question: Paul said he did not repent of his letter, though he did what?
explanation: Though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent.

question: Paul says they were made sorry after a godly manner so they might receive what from him in nothing?
explanation: Ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.

question: Paul says he wrote that what might appear to them in the sight of God?
explanation: That our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.

question: Before whom had Paul boasted of the Corinthians, and found it true?
explanation: If I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth.

question: How did the Corinthians receive Titus?
explanation: Whilst he remembereth the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him.

question: What does Paul say he rejoices that he has in the Corinthians in all things?
explanation: I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things.
